tools.name: exports_sources_get
tools.title: Search export sources for sellers and vendors
tools.description: Searches compact export source candidates for the selected seller or vendor. Requires sellerOrVendorIds from sellers_and_vendors_list and a keyword query. When multiple accounts are selected, only sources available to every account appear; search accounts separately if an expected source is missing. Keyword search across source names, table names, aliases, descriptions, and columns. This is not natural language search. Do not send a full question. Use one short Amazon or business term, for example ppc, roas, sessions, buy box, fba stock, payout. The source display name, table name, or source id returns that source. Inspect whyMatched to confirm the hit, then call exports_source_get before exports_create — this tool does not return columns. When the data scheme records issues for a table, the candidate includes them; treat deprecation and coverage warnings before creating an export. When a source lists relatedActions, load that type with actions_details_schema_get before actions_start. Rejects the request when any selected seller or vendor is still in FIRST_STAGE of initial load; wait until initialLoadStage is SECOND_STAGE or COMPLETE. When initialLoadStage is SECOND_STAGE, the summary includes a notice that historical data is still loading. When a selected seller sold products without COGS, or a vendor without a vendor code, in the last 30 days, the summary includes catalogCoverageNotice; profit and vendor_code columns are incomplete for those products until cogs_upsert or vendor_code_upsert fills them. Supports pagination via page and pageSize (default 8, max 12). Ranked hits are the starting points; an empty page does not mean DataDoe lacks the data — retry with a short term or a table name, or page+1 when meta.hasNextPage is true. Each source includes enabled: false when a user disabled the table; exports cannot be created from disabled sources. Each source also includes requiresDatePeriod (true means exports_create must send top-level from and to as YYYY-MM-DD) and exportRowLimits, the largest exports_create limit for CSV and for JSON on that source. defaultDataset: true means the table is required and cannot be turned off. retentionEditable and retentionDays show the organization's retention setting for the table from Settings > Data: when retentionEditable is true, retentionDays is the retention period in days and null means rows are kept with no time limit; when retentionEditable is false, retention cannot be changed for that table and retentionDays is null. accessAllowed: false means your roles do not allow data access or the table is disabled for a selected Seller or Vendor. The schema remains visible.

Use one short Amazon or business term, for example ppc, roas, sessions, buy box, fba stock, payout. The source display name, table name, or source id returns that source.

A column absent from the current page may still exist on another page. Required inputs: sellerOrVendorIds from sellers_and_vendors_list and sourceId copied from exports_sources_get. Call this after search and before exports_create. Rejects the request when any selected seller or vendor is still in FIRST_STAGE of initial load. When initialLoadStage is SECOND_STAGE, the summary includes a notice that historical data is still loading. When the source has COGS or vendor_code columns and a selected seller or vendor sold products without them, the summary includes catalogCoverageNotice. enabled: false means a user disabled the table and exports_create will fail until it is re-enabled. accessAllowed: false means your roles do not allow data access or the table is disabled for a selected Seller or Vendor. The schema remains visible. When relatedActions is present, load that type with actions_details_schema_get before actions_start. requiresDatePeriod: true means exports_create must send top-level from and to (YYYY-MM-DD); filters on the date column do not satisfy that requirement. exportRowLimits is the largest exports_create limit for CSV and for JSON on this source. defaultDataset: true means the table is required and cannot be turned off. retentionEditable and retentionDays show the organization's retention setting for the table from Settings > Data: when retentionEditable is true, retentionDays is the retention period in days and null means rows are kept with no time limit; when retentionEditable is false, retention cannot be changed for that table and retentionDays is null.

tools.name: exports_create
tools.title: Create a new export
tools.description: Creates an export job that runs a structured query against DataDoe's Amazon dataset for one or more sellers/vendors and produces a downloadable file (CSV or JSON). Required inputs: sellerOrVendorIds (from sellers_and_vendors_list), sourceId and columns (from exports_source_get after exports_sources_get — each source exposes its own column set; exports_source_get returns at most 40 columns per page, and the column set is incomplete until columnsMeta.hasNextPage is false), and outputType (CSV or JSON). When the selected source has requiresDatePeriod=true, from and to (inclusive YYYY-MM-DD on the source date column) are also required; filters on the date column do not replace them. Omit from/to when requiresDatePeriod=false and filter a time column instead. Optional inputs shape the query like SQL: filters applies row conditions before aggregation (WHERE); groupBy and aggregations create grouped results; having applies conditions after aggregation and accepts only groupBy fields or aggregation aliases; dateInterval (DAY/WEEK/MONTH) collapses a date group into that bucket; orderByColumn and orderByDirection sort results; and limit/skip paginate results (row limits depend on outputType and source). JSON exports support at most 1,000 rows; CSV exports support at most 5,000 rows. Raw Listings, raw Catalog, and raw Ads settings and settings history support at most 100 rows in JSON or 250 rows in CSV. Use limit and skip to paginate within these limits. HAVING requires at least one groupBy field or aggregation. Use filters for source rows and having for aggregate results. Both support and/or combinators and operators such as =, >, in, between, contains, and null. Returns an export id and a status. When a selected seller or vendor is still loading historical data (initialLoadStage SECOND_STAGE), the response includes historicalDataStillLoadingNotice because results may change as more data becomes available. Exports run asynchronously; status transitions from PENDING/PROCESSING to COMPLETED or FAILED. Completed exports expire 24 hours after generation. Poll exports_get to track status, then read the result with exports_raw_download (inline content) or exports_raw_url_get (download URL). If a query would exceed the row limit for its outputType and source, narrow it via higher-level aggregation, filters, having, or top-N ordering, or paginate with skip. Column names and source schemas are defined per source — use exports_sources_get and exports_source_get. For an offline overview of all tables, read the public Markdown data scheme at https://api.datadoe.com/api/v1/spec/data-scheme.md. Each export includes default utility columns that identify the seller or vendor and marketplace of each row. You do not need to request those columns. Some FBA sources have regional rows (attribution_method = 'regional') that belong to a whole Amazon seller account in a region (regional_account_id), not to one marketplace; their marketplace columns are null. An export includes each regional row once for any selected marketplace of that account and labels it as regional. Separate exports per marketplace each include the same regional rows, so do not sum them. MCP exports accept at most five sellerOrVendorIds per request. For more marketplaces, use batches with no overlapping marketplace selections. Keep marketplace-specific rows from every batch, but take all regional rows from only one batch per regional_account_id. Keep regional rows separate when aggregating so repeated rows are not included in batch totals. For a source containing only regional rows, select one marketplace per regional account.

items.description: Name of the column selected from the export source.

columns.description: Selected output fields. Can include source columns and aggregation aliases. Each export includes default utility columns that identify the seller or vendor and marketplace of each row. You do not need to request those columns.

from.description: Inclusive start calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) applied to the source date column in the marketplace local timezone. Required together with `to` when the selected source has `requiresDatePeriod=true`. Do not put the date range in filters; a filter on the date column does not replace `from`/`to`.

to.description: Inclusive end calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) applied to the source date column in the marketplace local timezone. Required together with `from` when the selected source has `requiresDatePeriod=true`. Do not put the date range in filters; a filter on the date column does not replace `from`/`to`.

filters.description: Additional row filters applied before aggregation, like a SQL WHERE clause. Do not use this for the source date period; send top-level from and to when the source has requiresDatePeriod=true.

field.description: Name of the column selected from the export source.

having.description: Post-aggregation filters, like a SQL HAVING clause. Each field must be a groupBy field or an aggregation alias. Requires at least one groupBy field or aggregation. Use filters instead for row-level conditions before aggregation.

field.description: Name of the column selected from the export source.

items.description: Name of the column selected from the export source.

column.description: Name of the column selected from the export source.

aggregation.description: sum requires a numeric column. min, max, and avg accept numeric or date/datetime columns. count/countDistinct accept any column.

orderByColumn.description: Sort field. Must be a source column or an aggregation alias or empty.

limit.description: Sets the maximum number of rows to return. JSON exports support at most 1,000 rows; CSV exports support at most 5,000 rows. Raw Listings, raw Catalog, and raw Ads settings and settings history support at most 100 rows in JSON or 250 rows in CSV. Use limit and skip to paginate within these limits.

skip.description: Optional zero-based row offset to use together with limit for pagination.

dateInterval.description: Use when groupingBy `date` column to have specific date aggregation, like changing day date to just month.

summary.description: Brief summary of the tool response.

isError.description: True if the tool response is an error.

tools.name: actions_details_schema_get
tools.title: Get details schema for starting an Action
tools.description: Returns the JSON Schema for the `details` object of a given action type required to start an Action, plus its access mode (READ or WRITE), whether it always requires Organization and principal PII access (requiresPii), whether that Action type is enabled for the Organization, and start tool (actions_start). When enabled is false, an Organization owner enables this Action type in the DataDoe app under Settings > Actions. A live start is rejected until then. A request with dryRun set to true still validates the payload. When requiresPii is true, the Action request, result, or generated documents contain personal data (PII). actions_start rejects it, including dryRun, unless PII access is enabled for the Organization and the principal has data.pii permission. DataDoe enables PII access on request. Conditional checks also apply when requiresPii is false: AMAZON_ORDERS_FIND with BUYER, RECIPIENT, or TAX includedData; AMAZON_MCF_DELIVERY_OFFERS_PREVIEW with a destination deliveryAddress or ipAddress; and AMAZON_FBA_REMOVAL_ORDERS_ADD with a return removalDisposition. Seller Central accounts support non-Ads listing, order, FBA, A+, and MCF action types. For accountType VENDOR (Vendor Central), non-Ads actions are limited to AMAZON_LISTINGS_UPDATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_UPDATE_VERIFY, AMAZON_LISTINGS_DETAILS_UPDATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_DETAILS_UPDATE_VERIFY, AMAZON_LISTINGS_CREATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_CREATE_VERIFY, AMAZON_LISTINGS_DELETE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_FIND, AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRODUCT_TYPES_FIND, AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRODUCT_TYPE_SUGGEST, AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRODUCT_TYPE_DEFINITION_FIND, AMAZON_APLUS_CONTENT_*, AMAZON_APLUS_MEDIA_*, AMAZON_SHIPMENT_TRACKING_SUBSCRIBE (US Tracking API only), and AMAZON_VENDOR_* purchase order Actions (Retail Procurement and Direct Fulfillment acknowledgements, shipments, labels, packing slips, invoices, and transaction status). AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_SHIPPING_LABELS_CREATE, AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_SHIPPING_LABEL_GET, AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_PACKING_SLIP_GET, and AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_CUSTOMER_INVOICE_GET require PII access. AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_CUSTOMER_INVOICE_GET is India only. Vendor Central rejects order, FBA, MCF, AMAZON_LISTINGS_RESTRICTIONS_FIND, AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRICING_UPDATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_FEES_ESTIMATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_FEATURED_PRICE_ESTIMATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_COMPETITIVE_SUMMARY_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_BALANCES_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_PAYOUTS_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_EXPECTED_PAYOUTS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_GET, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_DISMISS, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_GET, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_PREVIEW, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_ADD, and any other unlisted non-Ads action type. Amazon Ads action types apply to any Seller or Vendor with amazonAdsConnection, including accountType ADS_ONLY. If the action or feature you need is not found, you can open a ticket to the DataDoe team with datadoe_support_ticket_create. Group items into one Action. A standard read Action costs 0.5 AI Tokens for up to 100 items, then 0.25 AI Tokens for each additional 100 items. A standard write Action costs 3 AI Tokens for up to 100 items, then 1 AI Token for each additional 100 items. Each separate Action pays the starting price again. A dry run does not spend AI Tokens. FBA inbound Actions have fixed prices of 0.1 AI Token per read Action and 0.3 AI Token per write Action, regardless of item or shipment count. Campaign, ad group, target, ad, ad association, ad extension, portfolio, brand, and communication FIND Actions count as 1 item per call. Per-audience AMC prices and free AMC audience Actions stay the same. When a FIND Action's entity is in the DataDoe data scheme, use an Export or a BigQuery query. Use FIND only when you need live Amazon data that the warehouse does not have yet. One standard Export costs 2 AI Tokens. One integrated BigQuery query costs 0.2 AI Tokens. Compare the total cost of repeated FIND Actions with one Export or query.

AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_SHIPPING_LABELS_CREATE, AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_SHIPPING_LABEL_GET, AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_PACKING_SLIP_GET, and AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_CUSTOMER_INVOICE_GET require PII access. AMAZON_VENDOR_DF_CUSTOMER_INVOICE_GET is India only. Vendor Central rejects order, FBA, MCF, AMAZON_LISTINGS_RESTRICTIONS_FIND, AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRICING_UPDATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_FEES_ESTIMATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_FEATURED_PRICE_ESTIMATE, AMAZON_LISTINGS_COMPETITIVE_SUMMARY_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_BALANCES_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_PAYOUTS_FIND, AMAZON_FINANCES_EXPECTED_PAYOUTS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_GET, AMAZON_ACTION_ITEMS_DISMISS, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_FIND, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_GET, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_PREVIEW, AMAZON_ACTION_PLANS_ADD, and any other unlisted non-Ads action type. Amazon Ads actions require amazonAdsConnection (accountType SELLER, VENDOR, or ADS_ONLY with Ads attached). Each action type has a specific details schema, which you can retrieve with the actions_details_schema_get tool. Check enabled on that result before a live start. A live start is rejected when the Action type is disabled for the Organization. A start, including dryRun, is rejected when the Action is disabled for the selected Seller or Vendor. Users also need access through their roles. An Organization owner enables the type in the DataDoe app under Settings > Actions. A live write Action is rejected when the Seller or Vendor access level is Read only. Read Actions can run with Read only access. Set the access level to Read and write on the Accounts page to run write Actions. The access mode comes from actions_details_schema_get. An Action with requiresPii true is rejected, including dryRun, unless PII access is enabled for the Organization and the principal has data.pii permission. AMAZON_MCF_DELIVERY_OFFERS_PREVIEW also requires PII access when destination includes deliveryAddress or ipAddress. AMAZON_FBA_REMOVAL_ORDERS_ADD requires it when any removalOrders item has removalDisposition return. You can validate the request without creating or queuing the action by setting dryRun=true. A request with dryRun set to true still validates a disabled Action type. Listing VERIFY Actions (AMAZON_LISTINGS_CREATE_VERIFY, AMAZON_LISTINGS_UPDATE_VERIFY, AMAZON_LISTINGS_DETAILS_UPDATE_VERIFY, and AMAZON_LISTINGS_PRICING_UPDATE_VERIFY) call Amazon Listings Items with mode=VALIDATION_PREVIEW and return status, submissionId, and issues. They do not submit the listing. Amazon validation preview does not accept merge. DataDoe previews a merge with replace and the same values. The write still sends merge. dryRun does not submit the listing. It checks the DataDoe request and, for create, details, and pricing changes that include productType, the product-type schema. Preview before a write by running dryRun, then the matching VERIFY Action, then the write Action. One SKU per Amazon call. Limits count distinct SKUs; all changes for a SKU are validated together. AMAZON_ORDERS_FIND and AMAZON_ORDERS_GET_METRICS are a live preview of current orders. For large volumes and long-term analysis, use Exports or a direct BigQuery integration, which also refresh during the day. AMAZON_ORDERS_FIND accepts one search per Action. Its marketplaceIds can include only marketplaces connected as Sellers in the same Organization for the same selling partner. AMAZON_ORDERS_GET_METRICS fills marketplaceIds from the connection and uses from and to instead of an interval string. For campaign, ad group, target, and ad FIND actions, adProductFilter.include must contain exactly one ad product type; use separate requests to query multiple product types. One ID filter (for example campaignIdFilter) in these FIND actions can have more than 100 IDs; DataDoe queries them in groups of 100, and you page with the returned nextToken and the same query. AMC audience Actions (AMAZON_ADS_AMC_AUDIENCES_*, AMAZON_ADS_AMC_LOOKALIKE_AUDIENCES_ADD) need AMC enabled for the Seller or Vendor. Amazon builds an audience asynchronously and lists it in Sponsored Ads about 24 to 48 hours after it SUCCEEDED; DataDoe does not attach it later, so poll AMAZON_ADS_AMC_AUDIENCES_FIND, then get the audienceId with AMAZON_ADS_TARGETABLE_AUDIENCES_FIND and attach it with AMAZON_ADS_CAMPAIGNS_UPDATE audienceBidAdjustments or AMAZON_ADS_TARGETS_ADD. Details, flows, and best practices for Actions are available in the Actions documentation.

Waits up to 15 s for Amazon; AMC_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE is retryable with the same requestId. tools.name: amc_query_start
tools.title: Start AMC query
tools.description: Starts an on-demand AMC query (exactly one of workflowId, sql or templateId). Prefer a templateId from amc_query_templates_find over hand-written SQL. With templateId the latest template SQL runs; a template whose data sources the instance lacks fails with HTTP 422 AMC_TEMPLATE_DATA_SOURCES_UNAVAILABLE before any execution or charge. Requires Read and write access to the Seller or Vendor. Amazon limits: 30 ad-hoc executions/day per instance, counting every on-demand start (sql and workflowId; only schedule runs are exempt; reset time undocumented), and 10 executions running in parallel per instance (further executions queue). Over the daily limit the start fails with AMC_AD_HOC_LIMIT_REACHED (retryable later). Use on-demand runs for testing and one-off reports; recurring reports belong in workflow schedules. Starting is free and never checks the AI token balance; the first amc_query_result_get that returns download URLs is charged once per execution (List price 5 AI tokens, currently promotional 0). Failed and cancelled executions are free. outcome RESULT = known result; OPERATION = poll amc_operation_get until terminal. If recoveryStatus is AWAITING_CLIENT_PAYLOAD, resubmit the identical payload and requestId — do not start a second execution. Runtime depends on SQL (Amazon documents at least 15 min as typical; COUNT/simple aggregations can finish in under a minute). EXPLICIT timeWindowStart/timeWindowEnd are UTC instants regardless of timeWindowTimeZone. Cancel while delivery is WAITING if you do not want to wait. Raw SQL is never persisted.

tools.name: amc_query_result_get
tools.title: Get AMC query result
tools.description: Gets one AMC query result, including download URLs served by the DataDoe MCP server when delivery is AVAILABLE. Send a GET request to each files[].downloadUrl to receive the file (RESULT is CSV, METADATA is JSON). The URL requires no authentication headers and works until downloadUrlExpiresAt (5 minutes after this call, never past expiresAt); anyone with the URL can download while its issuer retains access. Call this tool again for new URLs. Files larger than 25 MB cannot be downloaded (HTTP 413). Aggregate or filter the query to reduce the output size. Requires a working Amazon Ads OAuth session for the binding, also while downloading. The first retrieval that returns download URLs is charged once per execution (List price 5 AI tokens, currently promotional 0); repeat retrievals are free. When the balance cannot cover that charge, no URLs are returned and the call fails with the same no-tokens error as other tools; the result stays available until expiresAt. Poll no faster than 5s. Runtime depends on SQL (Amazon documents at least 15 min as typical; COUNT/simple aggregations can finish in under a minute). rowCount may be null. failureReason explains FAILED executions (e.g. the SQL error). Empty privacy-threshold results are ordinary RESULT files and may include filtered_metrics_discriminator and filtered_reason columns.
